title: Glaciers and ice ages
examples: How does the weight of ice affect the landscape?
What is the difference between glacial and river erosion?
Can we tell from the rocks if an ice age happened here?

explain.say: Glaciers are huge, slow-moving rivers of ice.
As glaciers move, they scrape and pluck away rock material.
This scraping action carves out characteristic U shaped valleys.
Glaciers also deposit material when they melt, forming moraines.
Ice ages happen when global temperatures drop significantly over long periods.

items: What: Global cooling and ice advance

explain.say: In everyday life, glaciers shape coastlines by carving out fjords.

faq.q: What is the difference between glacial and river erosion?
faq.a: River erosion cuts V shaped valleys because water flows downward. Glacial erosion cuts U shaped valleys because the massive ice moves through the landscape.
asks: How does water carve land compared to ice?
What shape do rivers and glaciers make valleys?

faq.q: Are moraines the same as till?
faq.a: Moraines are specific piles of debris left by a glacier, while till is the general term for all unsorted material dropped by the ice.
asks: What is the difference between till and moraine?
What material do glaciers leave behind?

faq.q: How long do ice ages last?
faq.a: Ice ages cover vast periods of time, involving repeated cycles of cooling and warming over thousands of years.
asks: Is an ice age quick or slow?
What causes the cycle of ice ages?

faq.q: Do glaciers only form near the poles?
faq.a: No, glaciers can form in high mountain ranges as well, provided there is enough snowfall to accumulate over many years.
asks: Where can glaciers form besides the Arctic?
What conditions are needed for a glacier to start?

faq.a: Plucking is the process where meltwater seeps into cracks and freezes, breaking off chunks of rock that the glacier then pulls away.
asks: What is the ice doing to the rock?
How does the glacier break up the bedrock?

facts: Glaciers move slowly due to the immense weight of the ice above them.
Glacial erosion creates characteristic U shaped valleys, unlike river V shaped valleys.
Moraines are piles of rock debris deposited by melting glaciers.
Ice ages are periods marked by global cooling and expanding ice sheets.

quiz.say: What is the primary shape of a valley carved by a large glacier?
quiz.why: The massive, flowing nature of the ice carves a wide, trough-like U shape.

wrong.0: While some parts are irregular, the overall cross-section is distinctly U shaped.
wrong.2: This shape is typical of erosion caused only by running rivers.
wrong.3: Glaciers do not naturally carve perfectly circular valleys.

quiz.say: What term describes the unsorted material dropped by a glacier?
quiz.why: Till is the general scientific term for all the mixed, unsorted rock material left behind by ice.

wrong.0: Outwash refers to material carried away by meltwater streams.
wrong.1: Sediment is a general term, but till is more specific to glacial deposits.
wrong.3: Moraines are specific ridges of till deposited at certain points.

quiz.say: If a valley was carved by a glacier, what feature might be found at its end?
quiz.why: Glaciers often pile up debris, creating visible ridges called moraines at their edges.

wrong.0: Waterfalls are formed by rivers meeting different levels of rock.
wrong.2: Meanders are bends formed by rivers flowing across flat land.
wrong.3: Deltas are formed where rivers enter larger bodies of water.
